patch.summary:
Thesis: Same category, different company size — Both sit in business-communications, but documented company-size audiences diverge.

Same category, different company size. Choose Five9 only if your buying job matches “Cloud contact center (CCaaS) — Digital from $119/concurrent seat/mo; Core $159; Plus/Pro/E” rather than Grasshopper's shape. Choose Grasshopper only if your buying job matches “SMB virtual business numbers with extensions and apps — True Solo from $14/month annual (f” rather than Five9's shape. Workflow advantage: Five9 leans contact-center, sales-calling; Grasshopper leans business-phone. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Same category, different company size — Both sit in business-communications, but documented company-size audiences diverge.
- Positioning: Five9 is Cloud contact center (CCaaS) — Digital from $119/concurrent seat/mo; Core $159; Plus/Pro/Enterprise quote — 50-seat minimum.; Grasshopper is SMB virtual business numbers with extensions and apps — True Solo from $14/month annual (flat account, not per seat)..
- Company-size focus: Five9 (mid-market, enterprise) vs Grasshopper (solo, small-business).
- Workflow coverage skew: Five9-leaning contact-center, sales-calling, customer-messaging vs Grasshopper-leaning business-phone.
- Researched limits: Five9 — 50 concurrent-seat minimum — not viable for small SMB phone buyers; Grasshopper — Virtual-number / simple phone product — not full UCaaS (no native team chat or video meetings suite).

Limitations — Five9: 50 concurrent-seat minimum — not viable for small SMB phone buyers; Digital is non-voice; Core is the published voice+digital entry; Grasshopper: Virtual-number / simple phone product — not full UCaaS (no native team chat or video meetings suite); IVR, recording and simultaneous ringing require Solo Plus or above.

Poor-fit cases: Five9 is a poor fit when that limitation bites: 50 concurrent-seat minimum — not viable for small SMB phone buyers · Grasshopper is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Virtual-number / simple phone product — not full UCaaS (no native team chat or video meetings suite) · Avoid Five9 if you actually need Grasshopper's motion (SMB virtual business numbers with extensions and apps — True Solo from $14/month)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
